\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استعد} (istaʿadda)}{استعد (istaʿadda)}]{\ar{استعد} (istaʿadda) — to get ready}

\label{lesson:AR-C462-istaadda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to miss, then the Arabic for to waste time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استعد}}
\textbf{\ar{استعد}} — \emph{istaʿadda} — \textquotedblleft{}to get ready\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استعد} \ar{المسافرون} \ar{للرحلة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istaʿadda al-musāfirūn li-r-riḥla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The travellers got ready for the trip.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستعد}, \emph{yastaʿidd}.

It takes \emph{li-}: \emph{istaʿadda li-}, \textquotedblleft{}to get ready for\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استعد}} (\emph{istaʿadda}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-d-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to count\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, \textquotedblleft{}to make oneself ready\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaʿadda}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaʿadda}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaʿadda al-musāfirūn li-r-riḥla.} — The travellers got ready for the trip.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to miss, then the Arabic for to waste time, then say \emph{istaʿadda} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{استعد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To get ready\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اختصر} (ikhtaṣara)}{اختصر (ikhtaṣara)}]{\ar{اختصر} (ikhtaṣara) — to shorten; to cut short}

\label{lesson:AR-C462-ikhtasara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to waste time, then the Arabic for to get ready.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اختصر}}
\textbf{\ar{اختصر}} — \emph{ikhtaṣara} — \textquotedblleft{}to shorten; to cut short\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اختصرنا} \ar{الرحلة} \ar{بسبب} \ar{المطر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ikhtaṣarnā ar-riḥla bi-sabab al-maṭar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We cut the trip short because of the rain.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يختصر}, \emph{yakhtaṣir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اختصر}} (\emph{ikhtaṣara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-ṣ-r}, \textquotedblleft{}the waist\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII, \textquotedblleft{}to take in, to make short\textquotedblright{}, beside \emph{khaṣr}, \textquotedblleft{}a waist\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ikhtaṣara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ikhtaṣarnā ar-riḥla bi-sabab al-maṭar.} — We cut the trip short because of the rain.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to waste time, then the Arabic for to get ready, then say \emph{ikhtaṣara} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نفد} (nafida)}{نفد (nafida)}]{\ar{نفد} (nafida) — to run out}

\label{lesson:AR-C462-nafida}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to get ready, then the Arabic for to shorten.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نفد}}
\textbf{\ar{نفد}} — \emph{nafida} — \textquotedblleft{}to run out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نفد} \ar{الماء} \ar{في} \ar{منتصف} \ar{الطريق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nafida al-māʾ fī muntaṣaf aṭ-ṭarīq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The water ran out halfway along the road.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينفد}, \emph{yanfad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نفد}} (\emph{nafida}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-f-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to come to an end\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the plain verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to get ready, then the Arabic for to shorten, then say \emph{nafida} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اتسع} (ittasaʿa)}{اتسع (ittasaʿa)}]{\ar{اتسع} (ittasaʿa) — to have room for; to widen}

\label{lesson:AR-C462-ittasaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to shorten, then the Arabic for to run out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اتسع}}
\textbf{\ar{اتسع}} — \emph{ittasaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to have room for; to widen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لم} \ar{تتسع} \ar{السيارة} \ar{لكل} \ar{الأمتعة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lam tattasiʿ as-sayyāra li-kull al-amtiʿa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The car did not have room for all the luggage.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتسع}, \emph{yattasiʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اتسع}} (\emph{ittasaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-s-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be wide\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII; \emph{wāsiʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}spacious\textquotedblright{}, shares the root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ittasaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lam tattasiʿ as-sayyāra li-kull al-amtiʿa.} — The car did not have room for all the luggage.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to shorten, then the Arabic for to run out, then say \emph{ittasaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رفع} (rafaʿa)}{رفع (rafaʿa)}]{\ar{رفع} (rafaʿa) — to raise; to lift up}

\label{lesson:AR-C462-rafaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to run out, then the Arabic for to have room for.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رفع}}
\textbf{\ar{رفع}} — \emph{rafaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to raise; to lift up\textquotedblright{}.

\emph{rafaʿa al-ḥammāl al-ḥaqība ath-thaqīla.}

\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرفع}, \emph{yarfaʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رفع}} (\emph{rafaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-f-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to raise\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the plain verb; \emph{murtafiʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}high\textquotedblright{}, shares the root.

One more word for getting around.

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 455–462 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R462-review-455-462}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for a product and a brand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a product, a brand, a shop window, to display, a market stall
  \item volume, a variety, a sample, to fit, to be too tight
  \item a price cut, a voucher, to lower, to get cheaper, to spend money
  \item a guarantee, a rate, a commodity, to take back, to barter
  \item a consumer, a budget, expenses, purchases, to economise
  \item a breakdown, a malfunction, to get broken, to go bad, to suffer damage
  \item a cancellation, a postponement, to cancel, to miss, to waste time
  \item to get ready, to shorten, to run out, to have room for, to raise
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A product? (\textbf{\ar{منتج}}, \emph{muntaj}.) A brand? (\textbf{\ar{ماركة}}, \emph{mārka}.) A shop window? (\textbf{\ar{واجهة}}, \emph{wājiha}.) To display? (\textbf{\ar{عرض}}, \emph{ʿaraḍa}.) A market stall? (\textbf{\ar{بسطة}}, \emph{basṭa}.) Volume? (\textbf{\ar{حجم}}, \emph{ḥajm}.) A variety? (\textbf{\ar{صنف}}, \emph{ṣinf}.) A sample? (\textbf{\ar{عينة}}, \emph{ʿayyina}.) To fit? (\textbf{\ar{ناسب}}, \emph{nāsaba}.) To be too tight? (\textbf{\ar{ضاق}}, \emph{ḍāqa}.) A price cut? (\textbf{\ar{تخفيض}}, \emph{takhfīḍ}.) A voucher? (\textbf{\ar{قسيمة}}, \emph{qasīma}.) To lower? (\textbf{\ar{خفض}}, \emph{khaffaḍa}.) To get cheaper? (\textbf{\ar{رخص}}, \emph{rakhuṣa}.) To spend money? (\textbf{\ar{أنفق}}, \emph{anfaqa}.) A guarantee? (\textbf{\ar{ضمان}}, \emph{ḍamān}.) A rate? (\textbf{\ar{سعر}}, \emph{siʿr}.) A commodity? (\textbf{\ar{سلعة}}, \emph{silʿa}.) To take back? (\textbf{\ar{أرجع}}, \emph{arjaʿa}.) To barter? (\textbf{\ar{قايض}}, \emph{qāyaḍa}.) A consumer? (\textbf{\ar{مستهلك}}, \emph{mustahlik}.) A budget? (\textbf{\ar{ميزانية}}, \emph{mīzāniyya}.) Expenses? (\textbf{\ar{مصاريف}}, \emph{maṣārīf}.) Purchases? (\textbf{\ar{مشتريات}}, \emph{mushtarayāt}.) To economise? (\textbf{\ar{اقتصد}}, \emph{iqtaṣada}.) A breakdown? (\textbf{\ar{عطل}}, \emph{ʿuṭl}.) A malfunction? (\textbf{\ar{خلل}}, \emph{khalal}.) To get broken? (\textbf{\ar{انكسر}}, \emph{inkasara}.) To go bad? (\textbf{\ar{تلف}}, \emph{talifa}.) To suffer damage? (\textbf{\ar{تضرر}}, \emph{taḍarrara}.) A cancellation? (\textbf{\ar{إلغاء}}, \emph{ilghāʾ}.) A postponement? (\textbf{\ar{تأجيل}}, \emph{taʾjīl}.) To cancel? (\textbf{\ar{ألغى}}, \emph{alghā}.) To miss? (\textbf{\ar{فوت}}, \emph{fawwata}.) To waste time? (\textbf{\ar{ضيع}}, \emph{ḍayyaʿa}.) To get ready? (\textbf{\ar{استعد}}, \emph{istaʿadda}.) To shorten? (\textbf{\ar{اختصر}}, \emph{ikhtaṣara}.) To run out? (\textbf{\ar{نفد}}, \emph{nafida}.) To have room for? (\textbf{\ar{اتسع}}, \emph{ittasaʿa}.) To raise? (\textbf{\ar{رفع}}, \emph{rafaʿa}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
